q1.answer: ADR013 (node-fetch) is superseded and no longer in force; it was replaced by ADR014, which says Node.js code should use native fetch, but frontend plugins and packages (like this one) should prefer the injected fetchApiRef instead of a fetch library — matching the constructor-injected fetchApi in NotificationsClient.ts.

q2.answer: ADR007 requires that any fetch or XMLHttpRequest in tests be mocked using msw with express-style route handlers (as react-testing-library suggests), for all tests, not just this plugin. Compared to each test rolling its own mocking, this avoids inconsistent, one-off mocking implementations across unit/e2e tests and avoids mocking fetch/XMLHttpRequest directly in a browser-or-node-specific way.

q3.answer: ADR006 cites two technical problems with React.FC: it implicitly adds a `children` prop, and it does not support generic types on children. It also notes the concrete fact that Facebook removed React.FC from the create-react-app TypeScript base template because it was an unnecessary feature with next to no benefit.

q4.answer: ADR010 mandates Luxon as the replacement for Moment.js, giving two reasons Moment is being retired: it suffers from large bundle size and mutable-state issues, and the Moment.js project itself is being sunset (deprecated) with the maintainers recommending modern alternatives.

q5.answer: ADR004 (Module Export Structure) requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files down to the package's root src/index.ts. It was meant to make it easy to answer questions like 'Is the export in this module also exported by the package?' and 'What is exported from this directory?'.

q6.answer: No — applying ADR004's rule, notificationLinks.ts and plainText.ts are NOT part of the public API, because the rule states a symbol counts as exported only if it can be traced through an unbroken chain of index files up to src/index.ts; since there's no src/utils/index.ts (and src/index.ts doesn't mention them), the chain is broken, so per the ADR they are private by default even though nothing explicitly marks them so.

q7.answer: ADR011 defines x-react as the package for shared widgets/hooks that both the plugin itself and third-party frontend plugins can depend on. A -react package is only justified once some other frontend plugin actually needs to depend on notifications' components/hooks; today nothing outside this plugin reuses its code, so no x-react package is needed.

q8.answer: ADR003 allows a default export only when 'absolutely necessary', citing React.lazy modules as the one exception (React.lazy's dynamic import expects a default export). The workaround to avoid even that is wrapping the import with `.then(m => ({ default: m.Component }))` inside the React.lazy call, so the module itself never needs an actual default export.

q9.answer: That's ADR015. Its Consequences section says the loader/component option pattern will be applied to the new `@backstage/frontend-*` system APIs, but explicitly states existing APIs for the old frontend system in `@backstage/core-*` packages (which is the style the dev app predates/uses) will NOT be updated/retrofitted.
